articles.title: StarBlast
articles.summary: This article recounts an observing session at Fremont Peak where a 9-year-old, Larissa, was introduced to stargazing using a StarBlast telescope. With some guidance, she successfully located and observed 13 deep-sky objects, including several galaxies, nebulae, and star clusters. The latter part of the article provides brief observing notes for several other celestial objects like open clusters, a spiral galaxy, and a planetary nebula.

articles.title: Mid-summer Milky Way meanderings
articles.summary: This article encourages amateur astronomers to utilize the good mid-summer observing conditions by exploring a specific swath of the Milky Way, detailing various deep-sky objects. It provides practical observing notes for double stars, open clusters, galaxies, globular clusters, and planetary nebulae across constellations like Cepheus, Cygnus, and Aquarius. Additionally, the piece reminds readers about the upcoming CalStar star party and includes directions to a local observing site.

articles.title: Tim Thompson to speak at the August SJAA meeting.
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) announced that Tim Thompson of the Los Angeles Astronomical Society will be the guest speaker at their August 9, 2003 meeting. His talk, "Astrophysics, cosmology, and the age of the universe," will explore how stellar evolution, classical cosmology, and modern cosmology independently converge on an age of approximately 14 billion years for the universe.

articles.title: Why you see spots
articles.summary: The article explains the phenomenon of bright spots and halos on the Moon, addressing a reader's question about features near craters like Cayley and Dionysius. Author Dave North attributes these features to impacts exposing lighter, silicon-rich subsurface material that naturally floats above denser, darker layers, or through the formation of ejecta blankets. He also explores complex scenarios involving volcanic flows that can further enhance the brightness of these exposed or trapped silicic materials.

articles.title: The shallow sky
articles.summary: This article discusses the highly anticipated Mars opposition in August 2003, the closest in 73,000 years, noting early concerns about dust storm activity over Hellas but offering tips for optimal viewing, including filter use and resources for Mars maps and software. It also announces upcoming SJAA star parties at Coyote Park in August and September 2003, inviting the public to observe through telescopes. Brief updates on the visibility of other planets are also provided.

articles.title: CalStar 2003
articles.summary: CalStar 2003, an annual end-of-season star party hosted by the SJAA, is scheduled for September 25-27, 2003, at Lake San Antonio. The event focuses solely on astronomy and camaraderie, without formal speakers or prizes. Attendees can find accommodation options ranging from campsites to rental cabins, with a park fee of $32.00 per vehicle for the three nights.

articles.title: Board meeting synopsis
articles.summary: The SJAA board of directors held a meeting on June 14, outlining future club activities including a lunar eclipse star party on November 8 and Mars star parties in late August or early September. Key administrative updates included the plan to digitize all SJAA Ephemeris issues for the club's 50th anniversary, the appointment of Jim Bartolini as CalStar Czar, and Jack Zeiders being granted a life membership.

articles.title: SJAA loaner scope status
articles.summary: This article details the status of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) loaner telescope program, providing a list of scopes currently available to members, those recently loaned out, and those on extended loan. It includes contact information for Mike Koop to facilitate borrowing and mentions a waiting list for popular equipment. The document serves as an internal update for SJAA members regarding the availability of astronomical equipment.
